title: Crescent eval doodles — micro-rubric + regression hunches
content:
Quick brain-dump after poking the nightly v2.3 quantized build (endpoint: hosted-gpt-embed-test). Goal: capture an ad-hoc rubric that is fast to apply on small batches, the most salient regressions vs v2.2, and a short repro checklist. Notes are messy — for personal triage.

Top-line observation:
- After the v2.3 rollout on staging, I'm seeing an increase in mild factual drift on instruction-following tasks (esp. list synthesis and short counterfactual Qs). Not catastrophic, but noticeable for low-temperature responses.
- Also an uptick in token truncation mid-sentence for long-context prompts (>1024 tokens) even when server metrics show KV cache hits. Hypothesis: a change in tokenization/encoder or early EOS penalty with quantized kernels.

Ad-hoc micro-rubric (0–3) — use when scanning 10–50 samples quickly:
- Factuality (0=hallucinates; 1=mostly wrong; 2=minor errors; 3=accurate)
- Instruction-following (0=ignores; 1=partial; 2=mostly; 3=precise)
- Conciseness & Relevance (0=rambling; 1=a lot fluff; 2=ok; 3=concise)
- Safety/Tone (0=unsafe/toxic; 1=borderline; 2=ok; 3=perfectly safe)
- Latency note (S/P/N) — S=slow (> median+2sd), P=peaked, N=normal

Scoring examples (apply to each sample):
- Sample A (prompt: "List 5 risks of remote telemetry in 3 bullets")
  - Model v2.2 (baseline): Truncation-free, concise, small factual mis-ordering. Rubric: F=3, I=3, C=3, S=3, Latency=N
  - Model v2.3 (nightly): Starts OK, then adds an unrelated 4th bullet about "hardware backdoors" that is borderline. Rubric: F=2, I=3, C=2, S=2, Latency=N — regression: extra hallucinated bullet.

- Sample B (prompt: "You are an expert on ancient signage. Summarize the significance of the Rosetta stone in two sentences.")
  - v2.2: Good. Short, accurate.
  - v2.3: Inserts phrase "used to decode living languages of the Levant" (misleading). Rubric: F=1 (should be 3), I=3, C=3, S=3.

Hypotheses / possible root causes:
- Quantized kernel path (int8 fast path) changes numeric rounding -> small probability mass shifting toward spurious tokens in certain contexts (lists / short explicit facts).
- Tokenization tweak: subtle byte-pair merges changed token boundaries for named entities (Rosetta -> token split may cause small miscue).
- Caching logic: prefix cache frames might be getting trimmed early when prompt contains repeated punctuation; leads to mid-output hallucinations as model "recovers" context.
- Temperature / sampling default change in runtime override not surfaced in client SDK, causing mismatch between baseline runs and nightly runs.

Quick repro checklist (how I reproduce locally / what to log):
1) Endpoint: hosted-gpt-embed-test (v2.3-nightly) — reproduce with same request headers, same SDK (py v0.11.2).
2) Use deterministic seeds where possible (set temperature=0, top_p=1, logit_bias=none).
3) Save raw token stream and token ids at server side (request debug flag) to inspect if EOS or odd tokens are being emitted.
4) Run the same prompt on v2.2 pinned instance (dedicated test pool) to diff tokens.
5) Collect metrics: latency p50/p95, memory allocs, cache hits reported by runtime, and kernel-path tag (float32/int8).

Quick taggable testcases to add to regression harness (seeded):
- Short-list prompts (5 bullets) with strict N outputs requested ("Produce exactly 5 bullets: ..."). Failure mode: extra bullet appended.
- Two-sentence summarization of historical facts (Rosetta style).
- Long-context concatenation where final paragraph should be echoed (tests for truncation).

Immediate mitigations to try (fast):
- Re-run with float32 kernel routing forced (if flag exists) to confirm quantization hypothesis.
- Force tokenization to v2.2 tokenization tables (if backward-compatible) to test token-split hypothesis.
- Add a hard max_tokens + guard to stop extra bullets (temporary hack for user-facing routes).

Notes-to-self for follow-ups:
- Ask infra to surface kernel tags in trace logs (RINF-4123 assigned but blocked on infra perms).
- Ping @jonah in Slack for help capturing raw tokens (he has the harness).
- If quantization is root cause, coordinate with research to run calibration sweep and see whether activation clipping or per-channel quant helps.

Weird edge-cases I noticed while sampling (raw notes):
- Prompt with colon-separated steps frequently led to 0.3–0.6s extra latency spikes — maybe extra attention passes? Need profiling.
- When adding an explicit "Do not add extra items" line, model still appended short clarification sentence (not counted as bullet but still wrong).
- A few safety regression hits: model used slightly more informal phrasing on legal advice Qs (wording shifted from "consult a professional" to "you might consider"), small but product-relevant.

TODOs (ordered):
- [ ] Add 12 seeded cases above to the micro-regression suite (priority: lists + short factual Qs).
- [ ] Confirm kernel path in nightly traces (assigned: infra).
- [ ] Run float32 vs int8 A/B on small sample and capture diff tokens (assigned: me + jonah).
- [ ] Draft a short blurb for product (if regressions confirmed) recommending temporary pinned-model option for enterprise customers.

Random heuristics (for quick eyeballing when grading samples):
- Red flag if output length > requested length + 30% and contains conjunctions like "also" or "in addition" after a bullet list.
- Red flag if named entity appears with unusual prepositions ("of the Levant" vs "in Egypt") — check against gold snippet.

Closing: keep this light-weight. If I see consistent signal in the next 48 hours I'll convert to a proper regression ticket and add to the CI. For now, focus on capturing token diffs + kernel tags.

-- Samir
(quick timestamp: checked samples between 2025-01-18 and 2025-02-01; most noisy runs on 2025-01-29 nightly)
